plan.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: Regeneron's Phase 2 COURAGE final results. Lean-mass loss was 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo at 52 weeks (75 mg arm). Investigational, company-reported conference data, not yet peer-reviewed.
plan.angle: Title: 'Trevogrumab + Semaglutide: 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean-Mass Loss at 52 Weeks, Obesity (Phase 2)' (under 100 characters). First 15s: '42% less' means 4.2% vs 7.3% of lean mass lost at 52 weeks, 75 mg arm vs semaglutide + placebo, adults with BMI 30+. Company-reported at EASD 2026, in press at The Lancet, investigational. Lean mass is not pure muscle. No strength or function data yet. Pivot to protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training. Mention GI side effects. Exact prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Can Trevogrumab Stop Semaglutide Muscle Loss? 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean Mass in Phase 2
plan.why: Fresh Regeneron data (~Oct 1) with little creator coverage. It sits on one of the most-searched GLP-1 worries and fits our best long-form formula: a named next-gen drug decoded with its number and comparator. | fact-check: Checked against Regeneron's release from 1 Oct 2026 (https://investor.regeneron.com/news-releases/news-release-details/phase-2-courage-trial-confirms-trevogrumab-prevents-lean-mass; mirror: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/REGN/phase-2-courage-trial-confirms-trevogrumab-prevents-lean-mass-and-yckn8zkxi8ay.html). Lean mass measured by DXA at 52 weeks fell 7.3% on placebo + semaglutide, 5.8% on trevogrumab 25 mg + semaglutide and 4.2% on 75 mg + semaglutide. Regeneron calls that 20.5% and 42.5% 'relative preservation'. The population is adults with obesity (BMI 30 or higher). Results were presented at EASD 2026. Fixes: (1) The release says the paper is 'in press with The Lancet', so 'not yet peer-reviewed' is out of date. Say 'accepted by The Lancet, not yet published; figures from Regeneron's release'. (2) The release doesn't say the 25 mg arm 'was not significant'. Only say that if the release or paper states it; otherwise say 'smaller effect (5.8% vs 7.3%)'. (3) The release extract has no arm sizes, no total weight or fat loss per arm and no discontinuation rates. Use them only if a primary source reports them. Otherwise say 'not reported yet' and never estimate. (4) Adverse events: at least one in 77% on trevogrumab vs 82% on placebo + semaglutide. Most common: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting. (5) The thigh MRI figure (about 69-72% preservation) comes from a subset with usable scans; label it that way. (6) Don't echo Regeneron's 'prevents' wording, since lean mass still fell 4.2%. No strength or function data were reported. (7) Fix the title: 'Stop' overclaims. (8) Funder: Regeneron. The trial is investigational (trials only as of Oct 2026). Frame the STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 DXA anchors as separate trials. Keep the protein caveat for kidney disease.

package.description:
Did an experimental add-on cut lean-mass loss on semaglutide? Partly, and with big caveats.

Regeneron's Phase 2 COURAGE trial, adults with obesity: 4.2% lean mass lost on trevogrumab 75 mg + semaglutide vs 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo at 52 weeks. Company-reported at EASD 2026; Regeneron says the Lancet paper is in press. Lean mass isn't just muscle, and no strength data were reported. Common side effects: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting. Not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026; trials only.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
1. Phase 2 COURAGE Trial: Trevogrumab + Semaglutide — Regeneron, 2026: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/01/3373155/0/en/phase-2-courage-trial-confirms-trevogrumab-prevents-lean-mass-and-muscle-loss-during-glp-1-receptor-agonist-induced-weight-loss.html
2. Is Weight Loss-Induced Muscle Mass Loss Clinically Relevant? — JAMA, 2024: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2819410

script.working_title: Trevogrumab 75 mg + Semaglutide: 4.2% vs 7.3% Lean-Mass Loss vs Sema + Placebo, 52 Wks, Obesity
script.hook_pattern: Stakes + specificity: the first line names the drug, the 75 mg dose and the comparator, and gives the verified number (lean-mass loss down from 7.3% to 4.2%, 75 mg dose vs semaglutide + placebo, company-reported). The '42%' headline is decoded within 15 seconds. An open loop ('the one question this trial still can't answer') pays off in the 'What the headline leaves out' chapter.

scenes.narration: Semaglutide muscle loss is one of the biggest worries people have about GLP-1 medicines. Now, in a company-reported Phase 2 trial, an experimental add-on drug at a 75 mg dose cut lean-mass loss from 7.3% to 4.2% over a year, compared with semaglutide plus placebo.

visual.stat_label: Lean mass lost: 75 mg vs placebo arm

scenes.retention_device: Hook: stakes + specificity with named dose, comparator and exact number

scenes.narration: The drug is called trevogrumab. It's made by Regeneron, and in a Phase 2 trial called COURAGE, adults with obesity took it alongside semaglutide.
You might see this reported as 42% less lean-mass loss. Here's what that really means.
scenes.retention_device: Curiosity gap: decoding a headline number

scenes.narration: People on the 75 mg dose lost 4.2% of their lean mass in 52 weeks. People on semaglutide plus a placebo lost 7.3%.

visual.stock_query: two bar charts side by side

scenes.retention_device: Fast payoff of the hook number

scenes.narration: That's a gap of 3.1 percentage points. And 3.1 is about 42% of 7.3, which is why Regeneron calls it 42.5% relative preservation.
scenes.retention_device: Aha moment: relative vs absolute decoded

scenes.narration: One honest caveat up front: these figures come from Regeneron's own release. Regeneron says the paper is in press with The Lancet. And as of October 2026, trevogrumab is only available in clinical trials.

items: In press at The Lancet (per Regeneron)

scenes.retention_device: Builds trust with transparency before the deep dive

scenes.narration: By the end, you'll know the one question this trial still can't answer, and why it matters more for your daily life than any scan. Plus 2 things you can start today that have stronger evidence behind them.
scenes.retention_device: Main open loop + second open loop (2 things to do today)

scenes.narration: First, let's decode the word doing the heavy lifting in that headline: lean mass.
The body scan used in this trial is called DXA. It sorts your body into 3 buckets: fat, bone, and everything else.
Everything else is lean mass. That includes muscle, but also water, organs, skin and connective tissue.

visual.fact: Lean mass also counts water, organs and skin

scenes.narration: So when lean mass drops, it's not a pure drop in muscle. Some of it is the body adjusting to carrying less weight.
In a 2024 JAMA commentary, obesity researchers argued that some lean-mass loss is an expected part of losing weight, and that for many people it may not be clinically important.
But muscle still matters, especially as we age. Strength and balance help keep you walking, climbing stairs and living independently.
And that question is especially relevant on GLP-1 medicines, because they can lead to large weight losses in a fairly short time.
So how much lean mass do people usually lose on these medicines? 2 big trials give us rough anchors.
In STEP 1, adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition, and without diabetes, took semaglutide or placebo for 68 weeks.
scenes.retention_device: Micro-story setup of a landmark trial

scenes.narration: On average, they lost 14.9% of their body weight on semaglutide, versus 2.4% on placebo.
A small subset had DXA scans. Fat fell much more than lean tissue, so the share of their body made up of lean mass actually went up.
SURMOUNT-1 was a separate trial, of tirzepatide, in a similar population without diabetes. In its DXA subset, people lost 33.9% of their fat mass, versus 8.2% on placebo.

visual.stat_label: Fat mass lost, tirzepatide vs 8.2% placebo

scenes.narration: Their lean mass fell 10.9%, versus 2.6% on placebo.

visual.stat_label: Lean mass lost, tirzepatide vs 2.6% placebo

scenes.narration: Different drugs, different lengths and different people, so you can't line these numbers up against COURAGE. But the pattern is clear: most of the weight lost is fat, and a real slice is lean tissue.

visual.myth: These trials can be compared directly
visual.fact: Separate trials: different drugs, lengths, people

scenes.narration: That slice is exactly what trevogrumab is designed to protect. And to understand how, we need to talk about a very muscly cow.
Belgian Blue cattle are famous for their unusually bulky muscles, a trait called double muscling.
In 1997, researchers found the reason. These cattle carry mutations in a single gene, the one that makes a protein called myostatin.
Myostatin works like a brake on muscle growth. Earlier that year, the same lab showed that mice bred without it had individual muscles weighing 2 to 3 times more than normal.

visual.stat_label: Muscle weight in mice without myostatin

scenes.narration: Mice aren't people, though. Then in 2004, doctors described a young boy in Germany with a myostatin mutation and unusually large muscles.
That's a single case report, not a trial. But it hinted that the same brake exists in humans.
Trevogrumab is an antibody designed to block myostatin. The idea is to ease off that brake while semaglutide helps the body lose fat.
It's a neat theory. But does it hold up in real people losing weight on a GLP-1 medicine? That's what COURAGE set out to test.
COURAGE enrolled adults with obesity, meaning a BMI of 30 or higher. Regeneron sponsored the trial.

In the groups we're covering, everyone got semaglutide. On top of that, they got a placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. The trial also had other groups, including a separate part testing higher doses of 200 and 400 mg, and we'll come back to them.
scenes.retention_device: Clear setup before the scoreboard + small open loop (other groups)

scenes.narration: At 52 weeks, lean mass was measured with DXA. Here's the scoreboard.
Semaglutide plus placebo: lean mass down 7.3%.
Trevogrumab 25 mg plus semaglutide: down 5.8%. That's a smaller effect, which Regeneron describes as 20.5% relative preservation.
Trevogrumab 75 mg plus semaglutide: down 4.2%. That's the 42.5% figure you'll see in headlines.
On the DXA scan, 75 mg showed a bigger difference than 25 mg, the kind of dose pattern researchers hope to see in Phase 2. But as we'll see, the muscle MRI didn't show that pattern.

Regeneron also reported thigh MRI scans, which look more directly at muscle. In the subset of people with usable scans, it reported roughly 69 to 72% relative preservation, with both doses landing in a similar range: 72% on 25 mg and 69% on 75 mg.

visual.stat_label: Relative preservation, thigh MRI subset only

scenes.retention_device: New surprising stat + payoff of the dose-pattern tease

scenes.narration: That's a subset, not the whole trial, so treat it as supporting evidence rather than the main result.

visual.stock_query: small puzzle piece beside big one

scenes.narration: But a drug that changes muscle signalling raises an obvious question: what about side effects?
Here's what the release says. 77% of people getting trevogrumab plus semaglutide had at least one adverse event, versus 82% on semaglutide plus placebo.
An adverse event is any health problem during the trial, whether or not the drug caused it.

visual.stat_label: 1+ adverse event: trevogrumab arms vs placebo arm

scenes.narration: The most common were nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and vomiting. Sound familiar? Those are the classic semaglutide stomach effects.
In STEP 1, gastrointestinal side effects were reported by 74.2% of people on semaglutide, versus 47.9% on placebo. Most were mild to moderate and faded over time.

visual.stat_label: GI side effects, semaglutide vs 47.9% placebo

scenes.narration: Now, don't read 77% versus 82% as trevogrumab making semaglutide gentler. Without arm sizes and the full paper, that gap can't be interpreted.

visual.fact: Gap can't be interpreted without full data

scenes.narration: And 52 weeks is a short window for a drug like this. Long-term safety still needs larger, longer trials.

One more piece of context: other COURAGE groups that added a second experimental antibody, garetosmab, had many more people stop treatment because of side effects, and 2 deaths. Regeneron said it hadn't identified a causal link to treatment. A separate part of the trial also tested trevogrumab at 200 and 400 mg. None of those groups are in the results we've covered.
scenes.on_screen_text: Other arms: not in these results

visual.stock_query: separate trial group with caution sign

scenes.retention_device: Honest safety context; pays off the 'other groups' loop

scenes.narration: So the numbers look encouraging. But remember that question I promised? This is where it gets important.
scenes.retention_device: Calls back to the main open loop before the payoff

scenes.narration: Start with one word. Regeneron's release says trevogrumab prevents lean-mass loss.
scenes.retention_device: Chapter change, focus on one word

scenes.narration: But lean mass still fell 4.2% on the 75 mg dose. It reduced the loss. It didn't prevent it.

visual.fact: Lean mass still fell 4.2% on 75 mg

scenes.narration: Next, the release doesn't report how many people were in each group.
It also doesn't report total weight loss or fat loss for each group, or how many people stopped treatment. Those may appear in The Lancet paper. For now, they're simply not reported.

items: Weight and fat loss per arm

scenes.narration: Why care? If an add-on drug protected lean mass but changed how much fat people lost, the trade-off would look very different. Regeneron's 26-week interim results suggested fat loss went up, not down, but the 52-week numbers per group aren't out yet.
Here's the question this trial can't answer yet: did anyone actually get stronger, or move better? No strength or physical function data were reported.
scenes.retention_device: Payoff of the main open loop

scenes.narration: That's the part that matters in daily life. Carrying shopping. Getting up from a chair. Climbing stairs. A scan number stands in for those things, but it isn't proof of them.
scenes.retention_device: Short sentence rhythm, vivid everyday images

scenes.narration: It also tells us nothing about pairing trevogrumab with tirzepatide or other GLP-1 medicines. These results are with semaglutide only.
And this is Phase 2. Larger trials would come next before any approval decision. As of October 2026, trevogrumab isn't approved anywhere.
If you see anything sold online under that name, it isn't a safe or legitimate source.
But here's the good news: you don't have to wait for a new drug to start looking after your muscles.
scenes.retention_device: Positive turn, opens payoff of second loop

scenes.narration: Remember the 2 things with stronger evidence behind them? Here they are: strength training and protein.
In a 2017 New England Journal of Medicine trial, older adults with obesity followed a weight-loss diet for 26 weeks while doing aerobic exercise, resistance training, or both.
scenes.retention_device: Micro-story of a clever study design

scenes.narration: Lean mass fell about 5% with aerobic exercise alone, versus about 2% with resistance training and 3% with both combined.

visual.stat_label: Lean mass lost: aerobic vs resistance training

scenes.narration: That wasn't a GLP-1 trial, and everyone was 65 or older. But the principle holds up across research: muscles you use are muscles you're more likely to keep.
WHO recommends muscle-strengthening activity on 2 or more days a week for adults. Squats to a chair, resistance bands and wall push-ups all count.
Start where you are. If you're new to exercise or have a health condition, ask your clinician what's safe for you.
Now protein. When you're eating less, getting enough protein gives your muscles the raw material they need to repair and rebuild.
With a smaller appetite, it can help to eat the protein part of your plate first and spread protein across your meals: eggs, Greek yoghurt, fish, beans, tofu or chicken.

One important exception: if your clinician has told you to limit protein, for example because of kidney disease, follow their advice. Kidney guidelines caution against high protein intake for many people with chronic kidney disease.
And ask whether checking your strength or body composition makes sense for you, especially if you're older or already have low muscle.
Let's put it all together.
At 75 mg, trevogrumab plus semaglutide cut lean-mass loss to 4.2%, versus 7.3% on semaglutide plus placebo, at 52 weeks in adults with obesity.
It's company-reported Phase 2 data, with the Lancet paper still in press. There are no strength or function results yet, and key numbers are still missing.
Side effects looked like typical semaglutide stomach effects: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and vomiting.
Meanwhile, strength training and protein are tools you can use today.
If you're on semaglutide or considering it, remember this. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.
When the Lancet paper comes out, we'll decode the arm sizes, fat loss and dropout numbers this release left out. Subscribe so you find out whether trevogrumab's numbers hold up.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate overall and the sources are clean. I checked the COURAGE numbers against Regeneron's 1 Oct 2026 release and they all match: the population was BMI ≥30; lean mass fell 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo, 5.8% on 25 mg and 4.2% on 75 mg; Regeneron's relative figures are 20.5% and 42.5%; in people with evaluable MRI data, thigh-muscle preservation was 71.8% (25 mg) and 68.9% (75 mg); adverse events were 77% vs 82% with nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and vomiting most common; the paper is in press with The Lancet; and the release gives no arm sizes, deaths, discontinuations or strength data. The other studies check out too: STEP 1 (14.9% vs 2.4% weight loss; GI effects 74.2% vs 47.9%; DXA subset), the SURMOUNT-1 DXA subset (fat 33.9% vs 8.2%, lean 10.9% vs 2.6%), Conte, Hall and Klein in JAMA 2024, McPherron and Lee's 1997 mouse and cattle papers, the 2004 NEJM case report, Villareal NEJM 2017 (lean mass about 5%, 2% and 3%), WHO 2020, and the KDIGO kidney caveat. The prescriber line, the side-effect lines, the kidney caveat, the cross-trial framing and the not-approved date hedge are all there.

There's one scope error. In s52 the 26-week interim fat-loss result is presented as if it applies to the 25/75 mg groups. It actually came from the separate 200/400 mg higher-dose part of the trial (and the garetosmab triplet). Also, s51 says weight-loss results aren't reported at all, but the 2026 release does say lower-dose trevogrumab "did not meaningfully enhance the weight loss achieved with semaglutide alone." Both are quick fixes, plus a few minor qualifier fixes.

issues.claim: Regeneron's 26-week interim results suggested fat loss went up, not down, but the 52-week numbers per group aren't out yet.
issues.problem: Scope error. The 2025 interim (26-week) results that showed more fat loss came from the higher-dose part of COURAGE (trevogrumab 200/400 mg, with or without garetosmab), not from the 25 mg and 75 mg groups this video covers. As written, viewers will assume the 25/75 mg doses increased fat loss. The 2026 release also says lower-dose trevogrumab 'did not meaningfully enhance the weight loss achieved with semaglutide alone'.
issues.fix: Replace the narration with: "Why care? If an add-on drug protected lean mass but changed how much fat people lost, the trade-off would look very different. For the 25 and 75 mg doses, Regeneron says only that they didn't meaningfully add to the weight lost on semaglutide alone. The extra fat loss reported in 2025 came from the separate higher-dose groups, not these ones. Per-group fat-loss numbers aren't out yet." Change on_screen_text to "Fat data for 25/75 mg: not out". Keep source_ids S1 and S12.

issues.claim: It also doesn't report total weight loss or fat loss for each group ... For now, they're simply not reported.
issues.problem: Partly inaccurate. The release gives no numbers for total weight loss, but it does say qualitatively that lower-dose trevogrumab did not meaningfully enhance weight loss vs semaglutide alone. Saying weight loss is 'simply not reported' leaves that out.
issues.fix: Replace the narration with: "It also doesn't give total weight-loss or fat-loss numbers for each group, or how many people stopped treatment. It only says the lower doses didn't meaningfully add to weight loss. The numbers may appear in The Lancet paper." Change list item 2 to "Weight and fat loss numbers per arm".

issues.claim: other COURAGE groups that added a second experimental antibody, garetosmab, had many more people stop treatment because of side effects, and 2 deaths
issues.problem: 'Many more' gives no numbers, which breaks the rule that every comparison needs numbers. These are 26-week interim figures from the 2025 release (S12): 28.3% of the triplet group stopped vs 4–10% in the other groups. Coverage reports this as discontinuation, so say 'stopped treatment' without asserting that every case was because of side effects unless S12 says so.
issues.fix: Replace the first sentence with: "One more piece of context: in Regeneron's 2025 interim results, groups that added a second experimental antibody, garetosmab, had 28.3% of people stop treatment, versus 4 to 10% in other groups, and 2 deaths." Keep the rest as written.

issues.problem: The stat has no on-screen qualifier saying what it counts or which arm is which. The qualifier rule applies to on-screen numbers.
issues.fix: Change on_screen_text to "1+ adverse event: 77% vs 82% placebo arm".

issues.claim: In the subset of people with usable scans, it reported roughly 69 to 72% relative preservation
issues.problem: Accurate (71.8% and 68.9% among participants with evaluable MRI data). The stat label should say these are relative to semaglutide + placebo, so it isn't read as an absolute muscle change.
issues.fix: Change stat_label to "Relative preservation vs sema + placebo, thigh MRI subset only".

thumbnail.reasoning: All three candidates are legible at phone size with a single clear focal point (dumbbell mascot) and no cut-off or overlapping text. Candidate #1 ('42% LESS') best matches the title's headline-decoder format, which is InforMed's most repeatable winning formula for both Shorts (CagriSema, 53 views) and long-form (EloraTZP, 112 views — our best long-form ever). It converts the title's two raw percentages (4.2% vs 7.3%) into the single relative number already circulating in headlines, giving instant curiosity payoff plus a concrete, searchable hook. The small 'LEAN LOSS, PHASE 2' qualifier line keeps the claim honestly scoped without cluttering the big number. Candidate #0's 'Muscle Saver?' is a solid contrast visual but is vaguer and doesn't decode the specific stat, likely underperforming a number-led hook per our data (vague comparators underperformed in Shorts). Candidate #2's 'The Catch?' is a fine curiosity-gap option but is less aligned with the proven decoder pattern and could feel slightly like it's withholding the actual (strong, positive) finding. Given no thumbnail-specific signal yet in our data, defaulting to the format most consistent with what has repeatedly driven clicks (named-number decoder) is the safest high-CTR, non-misleading choice.

issues.claim: Trevogrumab Cut Semaglutide Lean-Mass Loss? 4.2% vs 7.3% Sema+Placebo
issues.problem: The 4.2% isn't tied to the 75 mg arm (the 25 mg arm was −5.8%), and the title leaves out the 52-week timeframe and the population. The packaging rules say titles must name the arm and the full population.
issues.fix: Did Trevogrumab 75 mg Cut Lean-Mass Loss on Semaglutide? 4.2% vs 7.3% Placebo, Obesity, 52 Wk

issues.problem: Both arms took semaglutide. A bare "vs PLACEBO" could be read as trevogrumab alone vs placebo.

issues.claim: Benefit stated; "Do protein and strength training already feel like enough for you?"
issues.problem: The comment states the benefit but not the side-effect line the script and description carry. It also mentions protein without the kidney caveat.
issues.fix: At 52 weeks in Regeneron's company-reported Phase 2 COURAGE trial, adults with obesity lost 4.2% lean mass on trevogrumab 75 mg + semaglutide vs 7.3% on semaglutide + placebo. Lean mass isn't pure muscle, and no strength data were reported. Common side effects: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting. Trevogrumab isn't approved; trials only. Which do you find harder on a GLP-1: strength training or getting enough protein? (If your clinician has told you to limit protein, e.g. for kidney disease, follow their advice.) Educational only, not medical advice. It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.
